initial_scene: The humanoid stands beside a light desk facing the desk and windows. A black tripod lies tilted on its side across the desk, with its legs already spread; both robot hands initially remain clear.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Initially clear; raises toward the near-side tripod leg.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Open and clear near the tripod head/column; proximity is not treated as contact.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod remains tilted on the desktop.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Moves onto a leg member extending leftward from the hub and closes over it; the exact first closure lies within this interval.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Open fingers remain beside the head/column without a demonstrated grasp.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod initially remains close to the desktop.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Maintains the grasp and begins raising the tripod; leg and hub follow left hand upward.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Remains visibly open near the head, then starts shifting down toward the legs; no early stabilizing role is claimed.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Whole tripod lifts and becomes more horizontal; spread-leg configuration remains visible.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Continues bearing the tripod by the same leg, maintaining object-relative hand placement.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Moves underneath another leg/frame member and curls toward it; by208–220 hand and that member co-move and support contact is evident.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod held above the desk, center column nearly horizontal; no independent head mechanism is manipulated.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Maintains its hold while the right hand changes orientation and finger closure.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Repositions from a flatter under-leg support toward a more enclosing grasp on a separate leg; visible change in palm orientation and finger arrangement across240,244,248,252,256,260,264,268. Complete loss of contact is occluded and not claimed.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod remains supported; modest whole-object orientation change accompanies the adjustment.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Retains the near-side leg grip and controls the lower/near portion as the tripod rises.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Encircles the separate farther leg near its middle; fingers visibly surround the member at340–350 and co-move with it through rotation.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Center column/head and leg assembly rotate upward together into vertical orientation. Already-spread legs stay open; no leg-extension, unfolding, dial, or head adjustment is established.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Maintains near-leg grasp while feet settle.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Maintains separate-leg grasp while feet settle.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod lowered into three-foot stance on desk.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Fingers open around416–424; hand remains near the leg briefly, then moves clear by446.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Fingers open around400–410; remains alongside its leg briefly, then moves clear around442–446. Support is not inferred once open solely from proximity.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod remains upright; hand opening and spatial withdrawal overlap, so no strict release order is asserted.

observed_sequence.left_hand: Withdraws and lowers away with visibly empty open hand.
observed_sequence.right_hand: Withdraws toward robot with visibly empty hand.
observed_sequence.object_motion: Tripod remains stationary and unsupported on three spread feet through final frame.

arm_hand_roles.left: Foreground anatomical left hand grasps one leg first, starts lifting before right engagement, maintains that hold through right-hand repositioning and whole-tripod rotation, helps lower the spread feet, then opens and withdraws.
arm_hand_roles.right: Farther anatomical right hand starts open beside the head without established contact, moves underneath a separate leg, repositions into an enclosing leg grip while left keeps holding, helps rotate and set down the tripod, then opens and withdraws.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: Sequential left-first engagement followed by right under-leg contact and grip repositioning; two-hand whole-object rotation/placement. No hand-to-hand transfer, human interaction, or visible mechanism adjustment.

anatomical_side_evidence.evidence: In the source first frame and native frames 70 and110, the robot faces toward the desk/window at image upper-left. The foreground shoulder and arm are attached to the lateral side toward image lower-left, corresponding to the robot left; the farther shoulder/arm lies across the torso toward image upper-right, corresponding to robot right. Continuous shoulder-to-elbow-to-hand attachment is visible.

outcome: The tripod is placed upright on the desk, both hands visibly release and withdraw, and it stands without hand support until the clip ends.
terminal_state: Tripod upright and unsupported on three spread feet on the desktop; both hands clear and arms lowered beside the stationary robot.
uncertainties: At320x568 native resolution, overlapping fingers, legs and braces obscure the exact segment inside the early right-hand contact. A separate-leg grasp is clearest after rotation, at340–370; no central mechanism grasp is asserted.

The right-hand adjustment at240–268 changes finger enclosure and palm orientation, but any complete momentary loss of contact is occluded. The prompt describes repositioning, not a full release and regrasp.
Both hands open and withdraw in an overlapping release phase. Exact last contact times and an absolute release order cannot be established from finger/object overlap.

Load distribution cannot be measured visually. Left-hand bearing before right engagement is supported by tripod motion with the left grip while the right remains open; later two-hand contact is supported by enclosure and co-motion, not mere adjacency.
annotation_discrepancies: No outcome discrepancy: the source instruction to stand the tripod upright on the desk is visibly fulfilled. The tripod is already on the desk initially; the observed action raises and rotates it there rather than transporting it from a separate location.
world_model_prompt: The humanoid grasps one tripod leg with its left hand and lifts the tripod from its tilted position. Keeping the left-hand hold, it brings its right hand underneath another leg, repositions that grip, and uses both hands to rotate the tripod upright and lower its spread feet onto the desk. It opens both hands and withdraws, leaving the tripod standing unsupported. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
original_task_instruction: This task demonstrates complex manipulation where the humanoid robot picks up a tripod and carefully stands it upright on the desk, requiring balance, precision, and spatial reasoning.

selected_segment.reason: Complete original single-task reference; no cropping or trimming requested.

bimanual_second_review.method: Same dedicated agent re-viewed all full-sequence stride-2 contact sheets, the original native first-frame PNG, final native frame and closely spaced native frames around contact changes; compared each hand separately against tripod hub, feet, leg segments and column/head landmarks.
bimanual_second_review.previous_prompt: The humanoid uses its left hand to grasp a near tripod leg and its right hand to support the central frame. Both hands raise and rotate the tripod from its tilted position into an upright stance, guiding its spread feet onto the desk. It releases the tripod and withdraws both hands, leaving it standing unsupported. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
changes: Corrected initial engagement to left-hand lift before right-hand engagement.
Replaced general central-frame right-hand role with under-leg engagement and a separate-leg grasp, including visible grip repositioning.
Removed unsupported strict release order and noted overlapping opening/withdrawal.
Confirmed whole-tripod reorientation, with no demonstrated mechanism adjustment or unfolding.
